title: Quasi-coherent module sheaves as cartesian families on all etale charts
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ with small etale ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_X)$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Work in a universe and small-skeleton convention as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Quasi-coherent module sheaves on a ringed site are defined by local presentations [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and module morphisms are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For each object $v:V\to X$ of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, specify a quasi-coherent module $F_V$ on $(V_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_V)$. For each morphism $f:W\to V$ over $X$, specify an isomorphism $c_f:f_{\mathrm{et}}^*F_V\xrightarrow{\sim}F_W$, where etale pullback is restriction on localized etale sites. Require $c_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ and $c_{f\circ g}=c_g\circ g_{\mathrm{et}}^*c_f$ under the canonical composition identification. A morphism between two such families is a family of module maps $h_V:F_V\to G_V$ satisfying $h_Wc_f^F=c_f^Gf_{\mathrm{et}}^*h_V$. Restriction of a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module to all these charts, with its canonical restriction identifications, is an equivalence to this category of cartesian families. In particular every such family comes from a quasi-coherent module on $X$, with compatible isomorphisms of its restrictions to the $F_V$, and compatible families of maps come from unique maps on $X$.

source.place: Tag 03LZ (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent-small-etale), together with Tag 03LY (lemma-characterize-module-small-etale); the compatible-map formulation is the categorical meaning of the description by data.

proof.text: Use the localized-site meaning of etale pullback specified in the statement and in [def-trf-algebraic-space]: an object $a:T\to V$ of $V_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the object $va:T\to X$ of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ over $V$, restriction of a module $M$ from $X$ has value $M(T)$, with the same ring $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ and the same restrictions, and the slice of $V_{\mathrm{et}}$ over $a$ is the slice of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ over $va$ with the same restricted ring sheaf. Let $M$ be quasi-coherent in the sense of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and fix such an object $T$. That definition, applied to the object $va$ of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, gives a covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ and exact presentations $\mathcal O^{(I)}\to\mathcal O^{(J_0)}\to M\to0$ on each slice over $T_i$. The same family is a covering of $T$ in $V_{\mathrm{et}}$, and these are literally presentations of $M|_V$ on the same slices, so $M|_V$ is quasi-coherent. Repeated restriction gives identical section maps, hence the canonical identifications satisfy the identity and composition conditions. Restricting module maps gives the stated compatibility equation. Thus the restriction functor in the statement is defined.

source.place: Tag 03LZ (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent-small-etale), forward construction; quasi-coherence of restriction to a localized site is local by sites-modules.tex Tag 03DL (definition-site-local)

proof.text: For a cartesian family $(F_V,c_f)$ define $F(V)=F_V(V)$, with its $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$-module structure. For $f:W\to V$ put $\rho_f=(c_f)_W\circ\operatorname{res}^{F_V}_{W/V}:F_V(V)\to F_W(W)$. Here $(c_f)_W:F_V(W\xrightarrow f V)\to F_W(W)$ uses the localized-site interpretation. Each $\rho_f$ is semilinear over restriction of regular functions, since the first factor is linear over $\mathcal O_W(W)$ and the second is a module-sheaf restriction. Therefore these maps have precisely the scalar compatibility of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 03LY (lemma-characterize-module-small-etale); explicit evaluation construction in sites.tex, lemma-glue-sheaves-absolute

proof.text: The identity condition gives $\rho_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$. For $g:T\to W$, naturality of the sheaf map $c_f$ gives $\operatorname{res}^{F_W}_{T/W}(c_f)_W=(c_f)_T\operatorname{res}^{F_V}_{T/W}$. Consequently $\rho_g\rho_f=(c_g)_T(c_f)_T\operatorname{res}^{F_V}_{T/V}=(c_{fg})_T\operatorname{res}^{F_V}_{T/V}=\rho_{fg}$ by the supplied cocycle. Hence $F$ is a presheaf of modules. For fixed $V$, the maps $b_{V,a}=(c_a)_T:F_V(T\xrightarrow a V)\to F(T)$ are linear bijections. For $k:T'\to T$ over $V$ the same calculation gives $\rho_k b_{V,a}=b_{V,ak}\operatorname{res}^{F_V}_k$. Thus $b_V$ is an isomorphism of module presheaves $F_V\simeq F|_{X_{\mathrm{et}}/V}$.

source.place: Tag 03LY (lemma-characterize-module-small-etale); expanded presheaf and localization checks in sites.tex, lemma-glue-sheaves-absolute

proof.text: Let $\{a_i:V_i\to V\}$ be a covering and let $s_i\in F(V_i)$ be a matching family. Put $t_i=b_{V,a_i}^{-1}(s_i)$. Naturality of $b_V$ identifies equality of the two restrictions of the $s_i$ on $V_i\times_VV_j$ with equality of the corresponding restrictions of the $t_i$ in $F_V$. The sheaf axiom for $F_V$ therefore gives a unique $t\in F_V(V)$ restricting to all $t_i$. Then $b_{V,\mathrm{id}}(t)\in F(V)$ is the unique amalgamation of the $s_i$. This proves the equalizer condition of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Along with the sectionwise module structures already checked, [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] now makes $F$ a module sheaf, and each $b_V$ is an isomorphism of module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 03LY (lemma-characterize-module-small-etale); sheaf-axiom verification expanding sites.tex, lemma-glue-sheaves-absolute

proof.text: For $f:W\to V$, evaluate $b_Wc_f=(f^*b_V)$ on $a:T\to W$. Its left side is $(c_a)_T(c_f)_T=(c_{fa})_T$, which is exactly the component of its right side. Thus $b_V^{-1}:F|_V\to F_V$ is compatible with every transition. To check quasi-coherence, fix any chart $V$. By [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], $F_V$ admits, on a covering $\{V_i\to V\}$, presentations by coproducts of the restricted structure sheaf. The isomorphism $b_V$ identifies $F|_{X_{\mathrm{et}}/V}$ with this very module on this very ringed site. Its presentations therefore give the local presentations required for $F$ on each $V_i$; no preservation-of-cokernels assertion is being imposed on section evaluation. Since this holds for every $V$, that definition says $F$ is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Tag 03LZ (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent-small-etale), reverse implication; sites-modules.tex, definition-site-local, clause (6)

proof.text: For a compatible family $h_V:F_V\to G_V$, set $h(V)=(h_V)_V:F_V(V)\to G_V(V)$. Naturality of $h_V$ and the given equation $h_Wc_f^F=c_f^G f^*h_V$, evaluated at $W$, give $h(W)\rho_f^F=\rho_f^G h(V)$. Thus these linear maps define a module-sheaf map $h:F\to G$ by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. On $a:T\to V$ the same compatibility equation reads $(h_T)_T(c_a^F)_T=(c_a^G)_T(h_V)_T$, so restriction of $h$ is the prescribed $h_V$ under the isomorphisms $b_V$. Componentwise identities and compositions are preserved.

source.place: Tag 03LY (lemma-characterize-module-small-etale), categorical morphism formulation; expansion of the omitted quasi-inverse details in sites.tex, lemma-glue-sheaves-absolute

proof.text: Starting from a module sheaf $M$ on $X$, restriction followed by the evaluation construction gives $F(V)=(M|_V)(V)=M(V)$ and $\rho_f=M(f)$, on maps as well as objects. Starting from a family, the maps $b_V^{-1}$ of step 5 identify its reconstructed restrictions with the original family, and step 6 proves naturality in family morphisms. These are inverse functors up to the specified natural isomorphisms. Uniqueness of a descended map is also explicit: a global map with the prescribed restrictions must have component $(h_V)_V$ at each object $V$, so all its components are forced. The resulting equivalence has both the object and map clauses asserted in the statement.

source.place: Tags 03LY and 03LZ (lemma-characterize-module-small-etale; lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent-small-etale), completed quasi-inverse and unique-map verification
